title: E minor chord (Em) from E major — left-hand lift and third-string emphasis
summary: This short JustinGuitar lesson demonstrates forming the E minor chord by lifting the index finger off the G string (the open G string marks the minor quality when the other fingers hold the E major shape). It emphasizes a common muting issue: if the third finger (ring finger) settles too flat, it can mute the G string and obscure whether the chord sounds major or minor. The instructor stresses keeping the index finger’s contact with the G string on the tip, so the G string can ring clearly, and notes that the critical cue for the Em sound is the ringing of the third string during any strum. The video then guides a quick practice check: when strumming, ensure the third string rings out rather than relying on a full six-string strum, reinforcing a practical approach to distinguishing E major vs. E minor by ear and finger placement during basic chord work.

sections.description: The video begins with the suggestion to base the Em shape on the familiar E major chord, then lift the index finger off the G string (3rd string) to make the G string open, creating the E minor sound. Viewers are reminded that the third string is key to whether the chord is major or minor, and that lifting the finger can introduce a muting risk from the other fingers if their positions shift.
